newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM SEES FLAT 1997 PROFIT EXCL DISPOSALS.
newsitem.headline: UPM SEES FLAT 1997 PROFIT EXCL DISPOSALS.

text.p: Europe's largest forest group UPM-Kymmene said on Thursday it expected full-year earnings to be about the same as last year, excluding gains from asset sales.
"UPM-Kymmene's financial result for 1997, before gains from asset sales, is still expected to be about the same as last year," UPM said in a statement with its first half results.
"Demand for printing and writing papers is expected to grow during the second half of the year, and the capacity utilisation rate will remain high," it said.

It said strong demand and a rise in pulp prices would gradually pave the way for higher prices, but "prices for magazine paper and newsprint will be lower than during the second half of last year", it said.
UPM also said demand for most of its packaging materials and special products was expected to remain strong.

In 1996, UPM posted a 3.56 billion markka profit before extraordinary items and it reported first half profit before extraordinaries rising 70 percent to 3.53 billion markka, with gains from disposals, from 2.08 billion a year earlier.
"Operating profit includes net profits of 2,106 million markka (vs 230 million in H1 1996) from the sale of fixed assets entered under other operating income," UPM said.
"Gains from asset sales, less the five-month operating profit for Rauma, totalled 2,852 million markka and losses 746 million markka," it said.
